queer_characters.name: Prior Walter
queer_characters.notes: Protagonist described as a gay man living with AIDS; centered sympathetically as the narrative's prophet figure.

queer_characters.name: Louis Ironson
queer_characters.notes: Described as Prior's lover who abandons him due to emotional overwhelm, a flawed and complicated portrayal.

queer_characters.name: Joe Pitt
queer_characters.notes: Closeted Mormon Republican attorney portrayed through shame and religious conflict; leaves his wife and becomes involved with Louis.

queer_characters.name: Roy Cohn
queer_characters.notes: Real historical figure depicted as a closeted right-wing fixer who hides his identity to preserve power and dies of AIDS; a deliberately villainous, self-hating portrayal grounded in history.

queer_characters.name: Belize
queer_characters.notes: Former drag queen and Prior's devoted, supportive friend; specific identity label not stated in source, inferred from description.

queer_creators.name: Tony Kushner
queer_creators.notes: Wrote both the original 1991 stage play and the television adaptation; no identity information provided in source text.

contributor_notes: Identity labels for Louis and Joe are drawn from the plot's explicit framing (lovers, closeted); Belize's specific label is inferred as source only notes former drag queen and friend.
